title: Large Language Models as a Semantic Interface and Ethical Mediator in Neuro-Digital Ecosystems: Conceptual Foundations and a Regulatory Imperative

bias_targets.methodology: Philosophical-ethical analysis and conceptual modeling of how LLMs, acting as semantic translators for Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs), might distort a user's authentic intentions due to embedded biases in training data and algorithmic priors.

Theoretical examination of the risk that LLMs may generate discriminatory, reductive, or stigmatizing interpretations of a user's mental states (e.g., pathologizing normal cognitive variations or misrepresenting emotional intent).

Conceptual analysis of the 'neuro-divide 2.0', evaluating how disparate access to high-quality, heavily personalized LLM semantic interfaces could exacerbate social inequality along cognitive and communicative lines.
